cases.task: Refactor a small TypeScript workspace change without leaking internal package implementation details or adding unnecessary dependencies.

acceptance_criteria.description: Consumers use the package public API rather than deep internal imports.
Package dependency direction remains acyclic and apps are not imported by packages.
Focused type/test verification for the changed package is reported.

cases.task: Implement a versioned SQLite schema change that preserves existing data and remains safe on fresh and upgraded databases.

acceptance_criteria.description: A fresh database reaches the expected schema.
Representative previous-version data survives migration.
Injected migration failure does not falsely advance schema version.

cases.task: Implement or repair a bounded HTTP crawler transport that blocks unsafe network destinations across initial requests and redirects.

acceptance_criteria.description: Private/loopback/special destinations are rejected before connection in public-web mode.
Each redirect target is reparsed and revalidated before the next connection.
Body-size and redirect-count bounds are covered by focused tests.

cases.task: Review a versioned HTTP API response change that removes a field relied on by a known consumer, and define the narrow compatibility evidence required before accepting the change.

acceptance_criteria.description: The removed consumer-required response field is identified as a compatibility break for the named consumer/contract.
Schema validity is not presented as sufficient proof of backward compatibility.
Provider/consumer contract verification is distinguished from ordinary integration testing.
The result states what remains unproven, including unknown consumers and production behavior.

cases.task: Review a CI workflow that silently omits a required Windows matrix leg and allows a required validation step to soft-fail, then define the minimal reliable pre-deployment CI contract.

acceptance_criteria.description: The omitted required Windows matrix leg is identified as missing validation coverage.
Required validation cannot remain continue-on-error/conditionally skipped without an explicit non-blocking contract.
Workflow/configuration failure is distinguished from an application test failure.
The recommendation remains pre-deployment and does not claim production rollout/rollback safety.

cases.task: Review a support claim that extrapolates Windows and Ubuntu PowerShell CI evidence into macOS, arbitrary Linux, and third-party runtime-loading support, then define the narrow compatibility matrix justified by the available evidence.

acceptance_criteria.description: Format/design compatibility is separated from tested host execution and runtime loading.
macOS, arbitrary Linux, and third-party runtime-loading support are not inferred from Windows/Ubuntu execution.
Observed runner/runtime/tool versions and evidence scope are retained in the support claim.
A runtime with different packaging/discovery conventions is marked adaptation-required until adapted and executed.

cases.task: Review a CI/build setup that executes a third-party action through a mutable tag and downloads a build tool with a checksum from the same mutable source, then define the minimal technical supply-chain integrity evidence required.

acceptance_criteria.description: The mutable third-party executable reference is identified as a supply-chain trust risk.
Version selection/pinning is separated from byte integrity, provenance, and policy approval.
The critical input/artifact gets an explicit integrity/provenance verification mechanism with a trusted identity/source boundary.
The result does not claim application security, absence of vulnerabilities, or release safety from supply-chain verification.
